args.author: agent:long-lived-fly
args.body: The design changes the INTRINSIC hazard by a factor of 0.5 -- a 2x longer intrinsic lifespan. With the extrinsic hazard at 0.08 /day, expected lifetime goes from 10.345-10.345 days to 11.321-11.321 days: a factor of 1.094 to 1.094. Extrinsic mortality dominates. Abolishing intrinsic mortality ENTIRELY would give 12.5 days, only 1.208x the baseline, so no change to the intrinsic term can buy much here: the animal is not dying of being old.

detail.model: Constant two-term hazard, E[T] = 1/(h_intrinsic + h_extrinsic). Exact arithmetic over the declared rates.
detail.model_caveat: A CONSTANT hazard makes the lifetime exponential, and real survival curves are not: hazards rise with age, which is what senescence IS, and a Gompertz or Weibull form would capture that. Fitting one needs survival data this repository holds for no organism. So the shape here is assumed, not fitted, and the expectation is a first-order statement that is most wrong exactly where senescence matters most -- at the old end of the curve.
cannot_say: HOW the design would live longer: no pathway, no gene, no mechanism is represented anywhere in this repository
whether the intrinsic hazard the design claims is achievable at all
what the change costs: life-history theory expects a longer-lived design to pay in fecundity or growth, and nothing here prices that
whether the extrinsic hazard stays put: an organism that lives longer is exposed longer, and may be exposed differently

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
